Windsor social worker guilty of child luring sentenced to 22 months

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:30
Instaread

The social worker had spent the past five months in custody at South West Detention Centre in Windsor.

By
Pascal Hogue
November 20, 2026 at 12:18 p.m.

A Windsor social worker convicted of child luring involving a 14-year-old girl he was counselling was sentenced to 22 months behind bars.

Shaun Raymond Ouellette, 47, was sentenced in Ontario Court on Wednesday for what Justice Christine Malott had previously called a “very serious offence.”

Ouellette was found guilty on one count of luring a child under 16 following a trial in June.

The Crown had sought the maximum sentence of two years less a day of imprisonment for the offence while defence lawyer Tasha Donnelly had asked for a conditional sentence of two years to be served on house arrest.

Court heard that Ouellette was the girl’s counsellor over a period of three months in late 2024. Ouellette, then 45, had been enlisted to help the girl, who was struggling with alcohol addiction issues.

What began as a “normal therapist relationship” between Ouellette and the girl evolved over time to include increasingly “luring behaviour,” assistant Crown attorney Kyrstin Krainz said during sentencing submission in September.

Ouellette’s communications with the girl became “progressively more sexualized, the contacts progressively (becoming) more personalized in the nature in which he reached out,” Krainz said.

Ouellette had conversations with the victim at night, which he encouraged the girl not to disclose. He also added the girl on Snapchat, attended her residence and supplied alcohol to her at two parties during that period, court heard.

At a second sentencing hearing in October, Ouellette, who has maintained his innocence throughout the court proceedings, said he had become “reclusive” in the two years since he was charged and described incidents in which he had been recognized and physically confronted in public.

“Part of me feels like I’ve been living a sentence for the last 22 months,” he said. “Seventeen months of that felt like house arrest to me.”

Ouellette had spent the past five months in custody at South West Detention Centre in Windsor. He called his time in custody a difficult but “humbling learning experience.”

Being in custody was “something I never expected,” he said. “A lot of the other inmates that are willing to talk to me, they say, ‘you don’t sound like you belong here.’ And I couldn’t agree more.”

Ouellette had spent the equivalent of 291 days in enhanced pre-sentence credit, leaving him with 391 days to serve on his sentence.

His sentence will be followed by three years’ probation. Ouellette has also been ordered to pay approximately $3,400 in restitution to the victim’s mother.
